Name: Achilles
Description: hero of the Trojan War

Name: Aiakos
Description: a king of Aegina, appointed as a Judge of the Dead in the Underworld after his death

Name: Aeolus
Description: a king of Thessaly, made the immortal king of the winds by Zeus

Name: Alabandus
Description: he was the founder of the town of Alabanda

Name: Amphiaraus
Description: a hero of the war of the Seven Against Thebes who became an oracular spirit of the Underworld after his death

Name: Ariadne
Description: a Cretan princess who became the immortal wife of Dionysus

Name: Aristaeus
Description: a Thessalian hero, his inventions saw him immortalised as the god of bee-keeping, cheese-making, herding, olive-growing, and hunting

Name: Asclepius
Description: a Thessalian physician who was struck down by Zeus, to be later recovered by his father Apollo

Name: Attis
Description: a consort of Cybele, granted immortality as one of her attendants

Name: Bolina
Description: a mortal woman transformed into an immortal nymph by Apollo

Name: The Dioscuri
Description: divine twins

Name: Castor
Description: The Dioscuri - One of the divine twins

Name: Pollux
Description: The Dioscuri - One of the divine twins

Name: Endymion
Description: lover of Selene, granted eternal sleep so as never to age or die

Name: Ganymede
Description: a handsome Trojan prince, abducted by Zeus and made cup-bearer of the gods

Name: Glaucus
Description: the fisherman's sea god, made immortal after eating a magical herb

Name: Hemithea and Parthenos
Description: princesses of the Island of Naxos who leapt into the sea to escape their father's wrath; Apollo transformed them into demi-goddesses

Name: Heracles
Description: ascended hero

Name: Lampsace
Description: a semi-historical Bebrycian princess honored as goddess for her assistance to the Greeks

Name: Minos
Description: a king of Crete, appointed as a Judge of the Dead in the Underworld after his death

Name: Ino
Description: a Theban princess who became the sea goddess Leucothea

Name: Tenes
Description: was a hero of the island of Tenedos

Name: The Leucippides
Description: wives of the Dioscuri

Name: Phoebe
Description: wife of Pollux

Name: Hilaera
Description: wife of Castor

Name: Orithyia
Description: an Athenian princess abducted by Boreas and made the goddess of cold, gusty mountain winds

Name: Palaemon
Description: a Theban prince, made into a sea god along with his mother, Ino

Name: Phylonoe
Description: daughter of Tyndareus and Leda, made immortal by Artemis

Name: Psyche
Description: goddess of the soul

Name: Semele
Description: mortal mother of Dionysus, who later was made the goddess Thyone (Θυωνη)
